title: Prom and Locker
premise: In the dying farm town of Halloway, Nebraska, closeted-by-circumstance Odile Thackeray finds her late grandmother's recipe box hiding instructions for a folk magic that lets the user take on another person's burdens—and their secrets. When Odile uses it to survive a brutal assault by the sheriff's son, they discover the town's founding families have been passing the recipes down for generations, feeding on the powerless to stay untouchable. As prom approaches and the recipes' final page demands a sacrifice, Odile must choose between becoming the town's next keeper of power or burning the whole inheritance down, knowing the magic takes something irreplaceable from whoever destroys it. In the end, Odile breaks the cycle at the cost of their own memories of the one person they love, walking into a future that is finally free but no longer fully their own.
about_author: Wendell Voss is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who grew up in a town smaller than the one in this book and never quite forgave it. They write about queer kids in places that were never built for them, and about the quiet violence small towns call tradition.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. While cleaning out her grandmother's house after the funeral, Odile finds a tin recipe box whose final card isn't a recipe at all but a set of instructions written in a hand that isn't Grandma's. The emotional beat is grief sharpening into unease—Halloway's kindness has always had a price tag Odile is only now reading.

chapters.title: Careful Is a Full-Time Job
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A day in the life of the only out kid in a town of nine hundred: the locker slurs, the forced smile at the diner, the sheriff's son Trace Delacroix circling closer. Odile tests the first recipe on themselves to erase a panic attack and it works—terrifyingly well. The beat is the seduction of relief.

chapters.title: What the Card Takes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Priya Chandrasekaran, Odile's best friend and the only person who knows about the box. They discover each recipe transfers something: pain, memory, guilt. Odile offloads their assault trauma onto a willing Priya and immediately regrets it. The beat is the first corruption—love bent into leverage.

chapters.title: The Keepers' Supper
chapters.summary: Trace's POV, the book's first villain window. Odile follows him to the grange hall and witnesses the founding families' monthly dinner, where an old woman visibly sheds decades while a farmhand across the room withers. The recipes aren't a secret; they're an institution. The beat is horror wearing a potluck's face.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Trace corners Odile after practice and, instead of violence, offers a deal: join the keepers, get protection, get out of Halloway alive. He reveals he knows what's in the box—and that Grandma Thackeray was a keeper who defected. The beat is temptation with a knife behind it.

chapters.title: Prom Court
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The keepers nominate Odile for prom king as a public test: accept the town's embrace or be marked. Meanwhile Priya, still carrying Odile's stolen trauma, starts unraveling. The beat is a masquerade tightening into a noose, with friendship fraying under borrowed weight.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Decoding Grandma's hidden annotations, Odile learns the final recipe, meant for prom night, requires a permanent sacrifice to end the keepers' line forever—and that the sacrifice must be freely given by someone the magic has already touched. The beat is dread becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Trace's POV. Trace, himself a kept boy—his father feeds on him—wavers as Odile quietly shows other townsfolk what's being taken from them. The town's consensus begins to crack. The beat is the villain's mask slipping to reveal another victim, complicating everything.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Under the gymnasium's paper stars, the keepers attempt the final recipe with Priya as the intended sacrifice. Odile interrupts the rite, claims the recipe's power, and turns it on the founding families, unmaking their stolen years while Trace holds his father back. The beat is righteous fury as climax.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The magic is dead, the keepers scattered, but the price comes due: Odile has lost every memory of Priya. Priya chooses to stay and be met again, introducing herself in the diner where they first met. The beat is bittersweet resolution—freedom won, love paid for, and a beginning disguised as an ending.
